verifiers.name: Spec fixture roundtrip
verifiers.description: A TXTAR fixture under test/spec/ that lowers a query to SQL and, where seeded, executes it against chDB and asserts on the returned rows.
detects: wrong SQL lowering
wrong result rows against a known seed
cannot_detect: semantic drift against the reference backend's own engine

verifiers.name: Reference differential
verifiers.description: Runs a query against both cerberus and the real reference backend (Prometheus/Loki/Tempo) over shared seed data and diffs the responses.
detects: semantic drift against the reference backend
cannot_detect: internal plan correctness independent of the final response shape

verifiers.name: Static invariant scan
verifiers.description: A source scan rejecting a forbidden pattern outright (e.g. a caching call site outside the one sanctioned result_cache stamp site).
detects: a forbidden pattern reintroduced at any call site
cannot_detect: a semantically equivalent effect reached through an undetected mechanism

verifiers.name: Go unit test
verifiers.description: A table-driven `go test` asserting a pure Go function's behavior directly (no chDB, no reference stack), run via `just test-unit` (go test -race ./...).
detects: logic errors in the function under test
boundary/edge-case regressions pinned by table-driven cases
cannot_detect: drift against ClickHouse's actual runtime behavior
drift against a reference backend's behavior

verifiers.name: Type-checked lint rule
verifiers.description: A golangci-lint rule (forbidigo, analyze-types: true) that resolves identifiers through Go's type checker rather than matching source text, run as part of the `lint` CI job.
detects: a forbidden symbol used anywhere in the scanned path set, including under an aliased import
cannot_detect: a differently-named accessor that reaches the same forbidden effect through a symbol not on the forbid list
a false-clean result from a local agent-worktree run, which this repo's own record shows can report "No issues found" without genuinely analysing — only a real CI `lint` job run counts as evidence

verifiers.name: Dependency graph lint
verifiers.description: The go-arch-lint tool, which parses .go-arch-lint.yml's declared component/layer graph and fails if an internal/** package is undeclared or imports across a layer boundary the graph forbids, run as part of the `lint` CI job.
detects: an internal/** package missing its component declaration
an import that crosses a forbidden layer boundary
cannot_detect: whether a package's declared layer is the RIGHT layer for what it does — that placement judgment is reviewer discipline
a false-clean result from a local agent-worktree run — only a real CI `lint` job run counts as evidence, per this repo's own operating record

verifiers.name: Property-based oracle differential
verifiers.description: A pgregory.net/rapid property test that draws a randomized or deterministically engineered dataset and query, evaluates the query against both cerberus's real HTTP handler (chDB-backed, full parse/lower/optimize/emit/execute pipeline) and an in-tree oracle, and shrinks any disagreement to a minimal reproducer.
detects: value-level divergence across a wide generated input space
a regression reintroduced into a previously-fixed bug class the generator's dataset specifically engineers for
cannot_detect: divergence in a shape the generator's grammar or dataset pool never draws — each gen/*.go file documents its own deliberate exclusions
drift against a real, separately-started reference server; the oracle here is in-process or hand-written, not the real backend (see VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL for that)

verifiers.name: Documented provenance review
verifiers.description: A hand-maintained provenance record — a doc comment or header file enumerating, entry by entry, which lines of a mixed corpus are copied from a third-party source and which are this repository's own additions — checked by a person reading the corpus against that record, not asserted by any script.
detects: a corpus entry's authorship being misattributed to the wrong source, when a reviewer actually cross-checks the documented list against the corpus file
cannot_detect: a new corpus entry added without updating the documented list — nothing scans for that drift automatically

verifiers.name: Reference status-code differential
verifiers.description: Fetches both cerberus and the real reference backend's raw HTTP response to a fixed, known-invalid request without the 200-only success fold every other differential pass applies, and asserts the two backends' status codes agree. The Loki and Tempo sibling passes (status_parity.go, compatibility/tempo/driver's `-- expect_status --` axis) express "both backends must REJECT this request the same way," which a body-diffing pass that folds every non-200 response into an UnexpectedFailure cannot express.
detects: one backend accepting a request class the other rejects, or vice versa
a shared rejection boundary silently drifting to a different status code on one side
cannot_detect: any answer-level drift for a request both backends accept — that is VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL's job
a rejection-reason mismatch when both sides already return the same status code for different reasons

verifiers.name: Ledger enrollment check
verifiers.description: coverage-package-floor.mjs, the cheap structural half of the coverage gate: it shells out to `go list` and `go tool cover` only (no chDB, no containers, no real test run) to find every package that carries statements in the full build, and fails if any such package has no committed floor file under test/coverage-floor/.
detects: a package with statements missing a coverage-floor ledger entry
a PR that lowers an existing committed floor
cannot_detect: whether a committed floor value is itself high enough to catch a real regression — the floor is a ratchet on the measured value, not an absolute correctness bar

verifiers.name: In-process forked reference evaluator
verifiers.description: Runs a query against the real upstream reference engine in-process, via a documented fork accessor (docs/upstream-forks.md) that supplies engine-internal state the harness computes itself as ordinary data preparation (e.g. nested-set tree numbering) rather than reimplementing the operator semantics under test. No live server is started and no wire/HTTP boundary is crossed — the harness constructs the engine's own internal representation directly and asks the real engine code to evaluate it, then compares identity-aware results (e.g. TraceID/SpanID) against cerberus's own answer.
detects: operator/evaluation-semantics divergence against the exact upstream reference implementation, independent of network or server variance
an identity-level (not merely count-level) mismatch in which specific records matched
cannot_detect: wire-shape or HTTP/gRPC-response-layer divergence — only a live, separately-started reference server (VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL) exercises the actual transport

a defect in the reference engine's own live OUTPUT that contradicts the reference engine's own documented, unit-tested semantics for the identical shape — an in-process match proves only that cerberus agrees with the reference SOURCE CODE, not that either agrees with what a live deployment of that same code actually returns

verifiers.name: Optimizer snapshot pair
verifiers.description: A TXTAR fixture pinning both the pre-optimizer and post-optimizer SQL and chplan-print snapshots for the same input plan (the optimized/unoptimized and chplan_optimized/chplan_unoptimized sections cerberus issue #3335 added, in test/spec/optimizer/ and, as sql_optimized/args_optimized, in every promql/logql/traceql fixture), generated by internal/optimizer's TestOptimizer.
detects: an optimizer rewrite changing the emitted SQL or plan shape in an unreviewed way for the fixture's own case
cannot_detect: two structurally different SQL/chplan pairs that are nonetheless semantically equivalent under ClickHouse's real execution
whether the optimized SQL actually executes to the same result rows as the unoptimized SQL — that is VERIFIER-OPTIMIZER-PROPERTY-EQUIVALENCE's job

verifiers.name: Admission wiring test
verifiers.description: A Go test that mounts a head's real HTTP handler (Mount) — or, for the /tail route, drives an actual WebSocket upgrade and frame exchange — onto a live httptest.Server with a real *admit.Limiter, and observes end-to-end admission behavior (the HTTP status/header or close frame a genuine client receives) rather than testing the Limiter type in isolation.
detects: a head's own mux wiring failing to invoke the limiter it was constructed with
a route mounted on the wrong budget (e.g. /tail drawing on the request budget instead of its own tail budget)
the wrong HTTP status, header, or WebSocket close code reaching a real client on rejection
cannot_detect: a defect in the underlying semaphore's own concurrency guarantees — that is VERIFIER-GO-UNIT-TEST's job against the admit package directly
gRPC transport wiring: this verifier only ever exercises a head's HTTP mux, never a real *grpc.Server

verifiers.name: Real ClickHouse integration test
verifiers.description: An integration-tagged (`//go:build integration`) Go test that dials a real ClickHouse server via testcontainers-go and observes server-side state — connection pool statistics and the server's own native-protocol session census — that no fake, chDB, or mocked substrate can produce, because the behavior under test depends on a live TCP session and clickhouse-go's real driver internals.
detects: whether a pooled ClickHouse connection survives or is destroyed by a given teardown ordering
a real driver/pool regression invisible to chDB (which has no connection pool) or to a fake cursor
cannot_detect: anything about cerberus's own in-process admission semaphore — this verifier never constructs an *admit.Limiter, so it proves nothing about admission-slot recovery, only about the separate ClickHouse connection a request's handler may have held

verifiers.name: Optimizer property equivalence
verifiers.description: A rapid-based property test (internal/optimizer/property_test.go, build-tagged chdb) that generates random plan trees and executes both the unoptimized and Default().Run-optimized forms against an ephemeral chDB session, asserting their row sets are equal.
detects: an optimizer rewrite that changes a query's real result rows for a plan shape the generator can draw
cannot_detect: a semantic drift confined to a chplan node kind the generator's narrow grammar never draws — internal/optimizer/property_coverage_test.go's uncoveredOptimizerKinds ledger names the current gaps
chDB-vs-real-ClickHouse execution drift: chDB is a coercive, not a strict, oracle for type mismatches production ClickHouse would reject

verifiers.name: chDB handler roundtrip
verifiers.description: A Go test that seeds a deterministic fixture into a real embedded ClickHouse (chDB) session, mounts a head's real HTTP handler (Mount) onto httptest.Server, issues a genuine HTTP request, and asserts on the DECODED WIRE RESPONSE — the full parse/lower/optimize/emit/execute/render pipeline, not a hand-built comparison string, a stubbed querier, or an internal plan/SQL snapshot.
detects: wrong resource- or attribute-scope projection reaching the real wire response
a schema override (a custom table or column name) the handler fails to honor end to end
cannot_detect: semantic drift against the reference backend's own engine — chDB is cerberus's own embedded ClickHouse, not a reference implementation (see VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL)
production-cluster-only behavior (a real clickhouse-go connection, cluster-specific settings) — see VERIFIER-REAL-CLICKHOUSE-INTEGRATION
